title: Sidecar normalizer + rate-smoothing for realtime console ingest
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Introduce a lightweight sidecar preprocessor that runs adjacent to the realtime ingest gateway. The sidecar will normalize incoming metric events (schema enforcement, unit normalization, timestamp correction), apply tenant-aware rate-smoothing to reduce burstiness upstream, and emit a compact canonical envelope to the main streaming pipeline. This reduces downstream pressure on continuous batchers and improves tail latency for high-cardinality tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary that can be deployed as a sidecar container to the ingress pod
Normalization rules implemented for current metric families (usage, errors, latency) with schema validation and clear reject path
Rate-smoothing module that enforces per-tenant token-bucket smoothing with configurable burst window and target QPS
Backpressure signals propagated upstream as standard 429/Retry-After headers and internal drop metrics
End-to-end tests demonstrating 40-70% reduction in peak load delivered to the main ingest topic under synthetic burst traffic
No data loss for steady-state traffic; documented graceful degradation when local buffer is full (emit sampled telemetry + tombstones)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — PoC normalizer in Go reading JSON lines and applying schema map (prototype repo: github.com/redwood/telemetry/sidecar-poC)
2026-03-05: Benchmarks show per-instance CPU < 12% at 5k events/s with small optimization; memory target 150MB
2026-03-12: Integration test harness created to replay tenant burst traces into sidecar + topic; observed 55% reduction in max per-second writes to Kafka-like topic
2026-03-13: Code review feedback from data-platform team addressed (idempotency header, tombstone schema); updating tests
decisions: Implement sidecar in Go for low goroutine overhead and existing infra libraries
Use protobuf canonical envelope for output to keep payload compact and schema-driven
Local smoothing uses a leaky-bucket with configurable burst allowance; smoothing window default 10s
Local buffer is an in-memory ring + optional spill to local RocksDB for OOM protection (configurable per deployment)
Backpressure exposed to upstream via 429/Retry-After and internal health probes; non-happy path emits sampled tombstones to downstream topic
tradeoffs: Sidecar adds operational surface area per ingress pod (deploy/upgrade complexity) vs huge reduction in downstream bursts
Using RocksDB spill increases disk IO but prevents data loss on extreme bursts; chosen as opt-in for resource-constrained clusters
Smoothing introduces a small added latency (median +5-25ms) but reduces tail latency caused by downstream queueing
Protobuf envelope speeds downstream processing but requires coordinated schema bumping during rollouts
test_plan: Unit tests for all normalization rules and timestamp correction edge cases
Property tests for idempotent envelope encoding/decoding
Integration tests: replay production burst traces (two tenant top-20 traces) into sidecar and assert downstream throughput reduction and no message corruption
Chaos test: simulate sudden network partition to downstream broker and assert graceful degradation path (sampled tombstones emitted)
Performance test: CPU/memory target under 10k events/s with varying tenant cardinality
rollout_plan: Canary deploy sidecar to 5% of ingress pods in staging for 48 hours
Run traffic replay and smoke tests; verify smoothing config via feature flags
Gradual ramp in prod: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with abort window and automated rollback on increased error budget consumption
Expose smoothing params as remote-config and runtime feature flags to tune without redeploy
Post-rollback monitoring checklist and runbook stored on Confluence
monitoring: Dashboards: Sidecar CPU/memory, per-tenant smoothing events, local buffer occupancy, dropped/sampled tombstones
Alert: sustained local buffer occupancy > 80% for 10 minutes (P0)
Alert: sidecar error rate > 1% for 5 minutes (P1)
SLO: < 0.5% increase in 95th-percentile latency for successful requests after sidecar is enabled
Traceability: add sidecar_id and smoothing_decision to tracing spans for downstream correlation
